bridgeRouteRisk.summary: bIB01 remains independently issuer-native and mintable on all seven authored token deployments; those native issuance rows stay canonical and outside Bridge Risk's bridge-control inventory. A separate six-chain BackedCCIPReceiver rail uses custody lock/release and Chainlink CCIP messaging against the native token addresses, with receiver owners, proxy upgrades, shared custody, router configuration, allowlists, and known router delivery contracts scored here. The CCIP DON/RMN/OCR validation domain is modeled separately because the reviewed record does not enumerate its validator roster, quorum, or controller. The shared custody address is a verified EOA, and each configured CCIP router is retained as a delivery contract rather than a validation authority; the delivery evidence is source-enriched, but the unresolved validation domain keeps this review blocked rather than cleared. The receiver source contains no bIB01 mint or burn path, and BSC has no current receiver deployment.

controls.label: bIB01 Chainlink CCIP DON/RMN/OCR validation domain

routeChecks.attestorQuorum: Chainlink CCIP's external validation domain includes DON/OCR consensus and Risk Management Network (RMN) controls for the reviewed custody lanes, but the exact production DON/RMN/OCR member roster, quorum, and controller were not enumerated; no threshold or custody claim is made.
routeChecks.trustedPeerOrRemote: The reviewed getRouter() reads identify the six per-chain Chainlink Router delivery contracts used by the BackedCCIPReceiver routes; those delivery identities do not identify the bIB01-specific DON/RMN/OCR validation authority.
routeChecks.unsupportedReason: The DON/RMN/OCR roster, quorum, and controlling authority were not independently enumerated. A Router delivery contract or Chainlink protocol label cannot stand in for a validator identity, so this shared validation-domain control remains unknown.

controls.evidence: The six reviewed BackedCCIPReceiver routes have known delivery and receiver identities. At Ethereum block 25771145, getRouter() returned 0x80226fc0ee2b096224eeac085bb9a8cba1146f7d, the receiver was unpaused, bIB01 was registered as 8492551 REGULAR, and custodyWallet() returned 0x5f7a4c11bde4f218f0025ef444c369d838ffa2ad; at Base block 50068162, getRouter() returned 0x881e3a65b4d4a04dd529061dd0071cf975f58bcd, the receiver was unpaused, bIB01 was registered as 8492551 REGULAR, and custodyWallet() returned 0x5f7a4c11bde4f218f0025ef444c369d838ffa2ad; at Polygon block 92147098, getRouter() returned 0x849c5ed5a80f5b408dd4969b78c2c8fdf0565bfe, the receiver was unpaused, bIB01 was registered as 8492551 REGULAR, and custodyWallet() returned 0x5f7a4c11bde4f218f0025ef444c369d838ffa2ad; at Arbitrum block 495307116, getRouter() returned 0x141fa059441e0ca23ce184b6a78bafd2a517dde8, the receiver was unpaused, bIB01 was registered as 8492551 REGULAR, and custodyWallet() returned 0x5f7a4c11bde4f218f0025ef444c369d838ffa2ad; at Gnosis block 47762958, getRouter() returned 0x4aad6071085df840abd9baf1697d5d5992bdadce, the receiver was unpaused, bIB01 was registered as 8492551 REGULAR, and custodyWallet() returned 0x5f7a4c11bde4f218f0025ef444c369d838ffa2ad; and at Avalanche block 92985493, getRouter() returned 0xf4c7e640eda248ef95972845a62bdc74237805db, the receiver was unpaused, bIB01 was registered as 8492551 REGULAR, and custodyWallet() returned 0x5f7a4c11bde4f218f0025ef444c369d838ffa2ad. These per-chain reads establish delivery contracts and receiver state only. Chainlink documentation describes a separate CCIP DON/RMN/OCR validation layer, but the 2026-08-28 review did not establish its bIB01-specific member roster, quorum, or controller. The Router contracts therefore remain delivery identities only; this validation-domain control is unknown and blocks a cleared bridge claim. Reclassified 2026-09-01 under AUTHORITY-LADDER 9.46: the controlling party for this control is the external Chainlink CCIP DON/RMN validation quorum itself, a rotating protocol-scoped operator set with no single controllerAddress to record. Its authority model is therefore validator-quorum — known but weak, graded no higher than a named issuer backend and never above a named multisig — rather than unknown. The unresolved roster, quorum, override and peer facts recorded above are unchanged; only the authority classification moved.
